data.one_liner: A grammar of data visualization and Flutter charting library.
data.what_it_does: Graphic is a Flutter charting library based on the grammar of graphics. It allows you to compose data processing steps and mark shapes freely in a declarative specification rather than being limited to preset chart types, supporting interactions and transition animations.
use_when: You need highly customizable and non-standard charts built on a grammar of graphics.
You require interactive charts with selections, tooltips, and scale transformations.
You want declarative chart definitions with entrance and transition animations.
avoid_when: You need a simple plug-and-play chart without understanding a visualization grammar.
You are looking for specific non-chart data visualization components not covered by basic marks.
strengths: Flexible declarative grammar derived from The Grammar of Graphics.
Highly interactive with event and selection definitions.
Customizable shape draw methods and mark transition animations.
weaknesses: Requires learning a specific grammar paradigm rather than traditional chart configuration widgets.
Documentation points largely to an external skill or example repository for deep usage.

alternatives.name: fl_chart
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer traditional, highly readable widget-based chart configurations instead of a grammar of graphics.

alternatives.name: syncfusion_flutter_charts
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a comprehensive, feature-rich suite of enterprise-grade chart types out of the box.

alternatives.name: community_charts_flutter
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want another declarative charting option previously backed by Google.
